{{Short description|On when elements of the 2nd homotopy group of a 3-manifold can be embedded spheres}}
{{about|embeddings of 2-spheres|the sphere theorem in Riemannian geometry|Sphere theorem}}

In mathematics, in the [[topology]] of [[3-manifold]]s, the '''sphere theorem''' of {{harvs|txt|last=Papakyriakopoulos|first=Christos|authorlink=Christos Papakyriakopoulos|year=1957}} gives conditions for elements of the second homotopy group of a 3-manifold to be represented by embedded spheres.

One example is the following:

Let <math>M</math> be an [[orientable]] 3-manifold such that <math>\pi_2(M)</math> is not the trivial group.  Then there exists a non-zero element of <math>\pi_2(M)</math> having a representative that is an [[embedding]] <math>S^2\to M</math>. This statement may be strengthened to show that the embedding is piecewise linear {{harv|Lickorish|1997|p=133}}.

The proof of this version of the theorem can be based on [[transversality theorem|transversality]] methods, see {{harvs|txt|last=Batude|first=Jean-Loïc|year=1971}}.

Another more general version (also called the projective plane theorem, and due to [[David B. A. Epstein]]) is:

Let <math>M</math> be any 3-manifold and <math>N</math> a <math>\pi_1(M)</math>-[[Invariant (mathematics)|invariant]] subgroup of <math>\pi_2(M)</math>. If <math>f\colon S^2\to M</math> is a [[general position]] map such that <math>[f]\notin N</math> and <math>U</math> is any neighborhood of the singular set <math>\Sigma(f)</math>, then there is a map <math>g\colon S^2\to M</math> satisfying

#<math>[g]\notin N</math>,
#<math>g(S^2)\subset f(S^2)\cup U</math>,
#<math>g\colon S^2\to g(S^2)</math> is a [[covering map]], and 
#<math>g(S^2)</math> is a [[2-sided]] submanifold ([[2-sphere]] or [[projective plane]]) of <math>M</math>.
 
quoted in {{harv|Hempel|1976|p=54}}.
